title: Level a floor sleeper: push a tapered shim under its low end until the bubble centres
instruction: Make the sleeper level with the shim, and leave the level on it.
context: Carpenters (SOC 47-2031, about 889,700 US jobs in 2025, BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook) level sleepers, sills, skids and cabinet bases most weeks by driving tapered wood shims under the low point while watching a level. The member has to come up off its bearing for the thin end to start, and the taper means every few millimetres of travel changes the height: a shim pushed too far lifts the member past level, one not pushed far enough leaves it low, and one caught under only the front edge bears on a corner. The job is done when the bubble sits between its lines with nobody holding the member.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up; arm bases at y +30.5 cm and -30.5 cm. (1) Two fixed 4x4 pads, 88.9 mm across (y) and 300 mm long (x 100 to 400 mm), brown. The far pad is centred on y -380 mm, its top 88.9 mm up. The low pad is centred on y -10 mm, its top 82.9 mm up: 6.0 mm lower, as on a floor that dips. (2) A loose 2x4 sleeper, 38.1 x 88.9 x 610 mm, spruce-pine-fir, 0.87 kg, standing on edge along y at x 300 mm, from y +170 to -440 mm. It rests on the low pad's outer top edge and the far pad's inner top edge, so it slopes 9.9 mm end to end, low at its +y end. (3) A loose 9 in torpedo level, 229 x 25 x 45 mm, yellow, 91 g, lying along the middle of the sleeper's top. Its top-read vial (green window) has two black lines 13 mm apart and a white bubble 8 mm long; the bubble shows the level's tilt (see fidelity) and lies between the lines when the sleeper is within 1 mm end to end. (4) A loose wood shim, 8 in (203 mm) long, 1-1/2 in (38.1 mm) wide, 3/8 in (9.5 mm) thick at the butt tapering to 1/16 in (1.6 mm) at the tip, 18 g, lying on the low pad along x on its centre line (y -10 mm), thin tip toward the sleeper and 2 mm short of its front face (x 281 mm), butt toward the robot, overhanging the pad's front face by 24 mm. Where the shim lies the sleeper's underside is 0.4 to 1.0 mm off the pad: the tip cannot get under without the low end lifted. The sleeper lies flush on the sloped shim, so its height is the shim's thickness at its rear face: pushed 151 mm past the front face (6.0 mm thick at the rear face) the shim carries the low end level; 137 to 167 mm keeps it within 1 mm, 122 to 184 mm within 2 mm; pushed fully home the sleeper ends 3.1 mm high. Lifting the low end needs about 4.7 N near its end (it pivots on the far pad). Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: End state, read at the last step from the poses of the sleeper, the shim and the level and from both grippers. Difference: the sleeper's end-to-end height difference, 610 mm times the sine of its long axis's slope. On the pads: the sleeper's centre line passes over each pad's top at that pad's centre line and the sleeper spans each pad's full 89 mm width (top view) and its lowest point is no more than 5 mm below the low pad's top. Shim under: the shim lies on the low pad (lowest point within 5 mm of its top, tilt under 15 degrees), its centre within the sleeper's length, its tip past the sleeper's front face and its butt short of the rear face (crossing under the sleeper, not beside or behind it). Full bearing: the tip past the sleeper's rear face and the butt still short of its front face, so the shim crosses the whole 38 mm width. Level on: the level's underside centre over the sleeper's top face (2 mm allowed), no more than 3 mm above it, its long axis within 10 degrees of the sleeper's. Hands off: on every step of the last 1 s both grippers' finger zones are 30 mm or more from all three parts, and over that 1 s each part moves under 1 mm and turns under 0.3 degrees. Score 0 if at any time the sleeper or the level drops more than 20 mm below the low pad's top (off the pads) or the sleeper turns more than 30 degrees off its edge, and 0 unless hands off. Otherwise: 1.0 on the pads, shim under with full bearing, level on, difference within 1 mm; 0.5 the same within 2 mm; 0.25 on the pads with the shim under, otherwise (pushed too far or not far enough, under only the front edge, level off the sleeper); 0 otherwise. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0. Sliding the sleeper along its pads is not penalised. Success: 1.0 held for 1 s. In a real trial, per condition: difference, the height of each end of the sleeper's top over the bench with a steel rule and a feeler gauge, or the bubble between its lines; on the pads, a rule from each pad's top to the sleeper's low end (5 mm) and a look from above for the centre lines; shim under and full bearing, a rule for the tip past the front and rear faces, a 15 degree angle gauge for the shim's tilt; level on, a 3 mm feeler under the level and a 10 degree protractor; hands off, a 30 mm spacer block against each hand, 30 fps video over the last 1 s, and a dial indicator on the sleeper's top (1 mm, 0.3 degrees: the bubble stays put); fall, the 20 mm drop and 30 degree turn by eye against a rule.
fidelity: Rigid bodies; the sleeper's 3 mm eased edges are square; the taper is one sloped slab over flat blocks. Friction 0.45 wood, 0.40 the level (est). The level's height (45 mm) and the vial's sensitivity are estimates. Declared rule: the bubble is a link on a slider driven each step to 1.5 m times the level's measured pitch, toward the high end, stopped at the vial's ends (a sensitive vial, est). The low pad is a block 6 mm shorter, standing for a floor 6 mm low.
reset_notes: Lay the sleeper on edge across the pads at x 300 mm, from y +170 to -440 mm, resting on both pads (it slopes, low at +y). Lay the level along the middle of its top. Lay the shim flat on the low pad along x on its centre line, thin tip 2 mm short of the sleeper's front face, butt toward the robot. Nothing is consumed; the shim is not crushed in the model, but a real one used several times should be swapped.
